speech.transcript: Substitution replaces each letter with another. The alphabet is scrambled, but the length stays the same. A substitution cipher maps plaintext letters to ciphertext letters. The key is the mapping itself. With 26 letters, there are 26 factorial possible mappings. Caesar cipher, shift every letter by a fixed key. Key three, meat becomes phhw. A becomes d, b becomes e, and so on. Mono-alphabetic, an arbitrary one-to-one substitution. The key is a permutation of all 26 letters, about 10 to the 26 possible keys. Playfair encrypts pairs of letters. Build a 5 by 5 grid from a keyword. Replace each pair using row, column, or rectangle rules. Hill cipher. Treat letters as numbers and multiply by a key matrix medullo 26. It encrypts blocks of letters at once. Substitution creates confusion. The relation between key and ciphertext becomes complex. Shannon's property of confusion is achieved by substitution.
